meta.what_this_is: A weights-based offer engine. Instead of a page of prose about what could be decided, each candidate change is scored against six factors, and the page computes and ranks with those numbers in front of the reviewer, who can disagree with the weights.
meta.open_problem_it_solves: The site could tell a reader where to click but not what to do next. Prose registers do not answer 'which of these should I do first'. A weighted score does, and it can be challenged factor by factor.
meta.how_weights_work: Each factor is 0-3 for every offer. The total is the sum of factor x weight. Effort is subtracted, because an offer that costs an owner weekend is not cheap because it would work. Nothing here is a forecast of revenue; every weight is a judgement and is labelled as one.
meta.unverified_rule: Any factor score that depends on information this repository does not hold is marked 'needs'. A 'needs' row is not scored as zero, because zero would read as 'no value'. It is shown as unknown and excluded from the ranking until the missing fact exists.
meta.method_source: Plain weighted-sum scoring. Arithmetic only; reproducible with python3 tools/page_offers.py --check.
meta.weight_change_note: unblocks-money was raised from weight 3 to 5 after the first run of this page. At weight 3 the ranking put the deploy-scope fix first, because OFF-01's owner-time cost outweighed its value. That was a scoring error, not a finding: an offer that decides whether ANY commission can be earned cannot rank below one that tidies what is served. The change is recorded rather than quietly made.

factors.label: Unblocks money
factors.question: If this is not done, can any commission be earned by any other work?
factors.why: The heaviest factor, because everything else is decoration if clicks are not credited. Weighted at 5 rather than 3 so that the one offer which decides whether any commission is possible outranks a set of individually useful improvements.

factors.label: Reduces a false claim
factors.question: Does this remove something the site currently asserts and cannot prove?

factors.label: Helps a buyer decide
factors.question: Does a reader choose better or buy faster because of this?

factors.label: Reaches new readers
factors.question: Does this make new people arrive from search or feeds?

factors.label: Owner time required
factors.question: How many hours or account logins does this need from the owner, not from a session?
factors.scale: 0 = a session can do it alone; 3 = needs the owner's account and real work

factors.label: Safe to reverse
factors.question: If it is wrong, can it be undone without losing money or trust?
factors.scale: 3 = trivially reversible; 0 = hard to walk back

offers.title: Confirm one Special Link in the Associates account and read the click report
offers.one_line: The only task on this list that decides whether the site can earn at all.
offers.what_changes: One product's link becomes an account-issued Special Link with a confirmed click. The other four stay as they are until it works.
offers.evidence_for: Program Policies 2(a): 'Special Links enable accurate tracking, reporting, and accrual of commission income.' Nothing in this repository can see the report.
offers.owner_does: Sign in, open Associates Central, generate one link, click it once, read the report.
offers.if_it_fails: Nothing on the site breaks; the register records 'tried, no click credited' and the site's position becomes known rather than assumed.

offers.title: Fix the deploy scope so the published site is only the published site
offers.one_line: Stop serving the build scripts, the data registers and five retired storefronts.
offers.what_changes: Pages switches from 'deploy from the repository root' to the staged artefact, so /tools/, /src/, /archive/ and the retired editions stop resolving.
offers.evidence_for: This session fetched the live https://karagemop466-tech.github.io/Affil1/tools/build.py and .../archive/notes-edition/index.html. Both returned 200 with content. github pages API reports build_type legacy, source.path '/'.
offers.owner_does: Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions (one dropdown), or fix the path so the staged directory is what is served.
offers.if_it_fails: The site would go offline if the workflow is misconfigured; the previous commit stays deployable until it is right, and the owner should verify before closing the tab.
offers.blocks: Every 'one site to index' claim the brief makes.

offers.title: Stop asserting a tagged relationship until it is confirmed
offers.one_line: Either confirm the tag, or ship untagged reference links and say so.
offers.what_changes: The build stops adding ?tag= from a fallback. Buy links stay, but they become honest reference links until OFF-01 lands.
offers.evidence_for: tools/paid_link_gate.py is the gate that is supposed to decide this. tools/validate.py does not import it. The generated pages publish the tag anyway. The disclosure strip says 'this site may earn a commission'.
offers.owner_does: Nothing — a session can do it. It is listed because it changes what the site claims.
offers.if_it_fails: Removing the tag reduces nothing if the tag was never credited, which is the current state, and is restored in one line once OFF-01 confirms.
offers.blocks: Nothing, but it is the safest default while OFF-01 is open.

offers.title: Give every product page an add-to-basket path
offers.one_line: A reader who has decided should not have to hunt for the button.
offers.what_changes: Cart permalinks replace the single 'See it on Amazon' call to action, with the buyer note kept as the second door.
offers.evidence_for: This session opened the add.html endpoint and reached Amazon's sign-in redirect with the Associates return path, so the format is accepted. Without it, every click costs the reader a second decision.
offers.owner_does: Nothing — implemented in this session for the front page.
offers.if_it_fails: The detail-page link is still beside it, so a reader is never stranded.
offers.blocks: Conversion measurement, because the event only exists once the CTA exists.

offers.title: Replace the photoreal holiday feature with a consistent illustration
offers.one_line: The one section built to feel like a real publication has the one image that breaks the rule.
offers.what_changes: Either a licensed photograph with recorded provenance, or a re-drawn illustration in the same visual language as the other seven.
offers.evidence_for: This session opened assets/img/holiday-hosting-counter-w900.jpg: it is a photorealistic kitchen photograph with warm light and a bokeh window. Every other image on the site is an engraving or wash drawing. src/data/images.json states the rule as illustrative-only; FLG-020 records that this asset has no origin.
offers.owner_does: Choose: licence a real photo, or commission the drawing. A session can draw; only the owner can licence.
offers.if_it_fails: Doing nothing keeps a small inconsistency, not a false product claim, because the caption does not say it is a photograph of P-02.

offers.title: Publish one guide, then read the queries before choosing the next
offers.one_line: Write where the evidence points, not where instinct does.
offers.what_changes: A fortnightly guide, each added to the sitemap and the feed, with the next topic chosen from Search Console queries rather than guesswork.
offers.evidence_for: The nine existing guides already cover the four question-shaped topics the brief suggested. Without a query report, a tenth is a guess. Q-07 and S-07 are both open on exactly this.
offers.owner_does: Verify the Search Console property once, and hand over read access or a screenshot.
offers.if_it_fails: A guide that nobody reads costs writing time, not correctness, and is reversible by unlisting it.
offers.blocks: Topic selection, and therefore most of the content plan.

offers.title: Put a named human on the masthead
offers.one_line: Or stop implying one is behind the notes.
offers.what_changes: A real byline with two true sentences, or an explicit 'anonymous desk' statement on every page.
offers.evidence_for: FTC Endorsement Guides FAQ: an endorsement should reflect the honest opinion of the endorser. A site that reads like an experienced kitchen editor but names nobody is implying an endorser it does not have.
offers.owner_does: Supply a name and two true sentences, or approve the anonymous-desk wording.
offers.if_it_fails: An invented persona would be worse than the current state, so the fallback is the explicit statement, not a plausible name.
offers.blocks: Photography, first-hand testing, and any hands-on content.

offers.title: Point a real analytics endpoint at the five defined events
offers.one_line: Measure before optimising, and measure the events the pages actually fire.
offers.what_changes: A self-hosted collector receives page_view, product_click, cart_click, guide_read and search_intent, with no cookies and no third-party script.
offers.evidence_for: assets/js/analytics.js already emits the five events into a queue that has no endpoint. Leaving it inert means the next decision is made blind.
offers.owner_does: Choose a host and a retention period, or accept the anonymous aggregate-only fallback.
offers.if_it_fails: The queue stays inert; nothing breaks.
offers.blocks: Any claim about what readers do.

offers.title: Move off the repository subpath to an owned domain
offers.one_line: A shop at a /Affil1/ path is a shop in a corridor.
offers.what_changes: Every canonical, the sitemap, the feed and the OG images point at one domain the owner controls.
offers.evidence_for: Pages serves this project from karagemop466-tech.github.io/Affil1/. Canonical URLs, the sitemap and the feed all hardcode that subpath, which means any future move rewrites every page at once.
offers.owner_does: Buy a domain and add a CNAME. The DNS and the certificate take a day.
offers.if_it_fails: A wrong DNS record takes the site down until it is corrected; the github.io address keeps working meanwhile if configured sequentially.
offers.blocks: Serious outreach, because a review site on a repo subpath looks like a test.

offers.title: Get ten qualifying sales before relying on the Creators API
offers.one_line: The price feed is not a build task; it is a consequence of selling.
offers.what_changes: Nothing yet. It records the order of operations so no session builds a price feature that cannot be fed.
offers.evidence_for: Program Policies 2(b) permits prices only from an Amazon-served link or from the APIs. FLG-022 records that PA-API 5 is deprecated and the Creators API needs at least 10 qualifying sales in the past 30 days.
offers.owner_does: Sell ten things first. Nothing in a repository can shortcut this.
offers.if_it_fails: No fallback is needed; the site simply shows no prices, which is its current and permitted state.
offers.blocks: Any price, rating or availability display.

paths.name: Make it earn
paths.summary: Prove one link pays before improving anything else.
paths.why: Three of the ten offers touch whether money can arrive. The rest touch whether it arrives faster or from further away.
paths.cost: One owner session in Associates Central.

paths.name: Make it honest
paths.summary: Remove the claims the repository cannot support, in the cheapest order.
paths.why: Each of these deletes an assertion the site currently makes and cannot prove. None of them needs new content.
paths.cost: One Pages setting, one image, two sentences.

paths.name: Make it found
paths.summary: Fix the address, verify the property, then write where the queries say.
paths.why: Search traffic is the only channel that compounds, and it needs a stable address and a report to read.
paths.cost: A domain, a verification, and a publishing rhythm.
